title: The topping basket
scenario: A helper adds a topping to a pizza. A fresh pizza should start with NO toppings every call.

intro.job: A helper adds a topping to a pizza. A fresh pizza should start with NO toppings every call.

idea.rule: A default list is built ONCE and shared forever — defaults should be things that never change.
idea.detail: Python builds a function's default values one time, when the def line runs — not each call. A default list is therefore the same list on every call, and append keeps adding to it. The safe pattern: default to None, and build a new list inside the function.

model_restatement: Call add once per topping, each time with a brand-new empty tray, and print the trays.

clarify.question: Will callers ever pass their own tray?
clarify.answer: Sometimes — but today every call uses the default.

clarify.question: What if there are no toppings?
clarify.answer: Then no trays: an empty list.

clarify.question: What should be printed?
clarify.answer: The list of trays the calls handed back.

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Write add(item, tray) with an empty tray as the default; put the topping in and hand the tray back. Call it once per topping and print the trays.
draft_code:
def add(item, tray=[]):
    tray.append(item)
    return tray
results = []
for it in toppings:
    results.append(add(it))
print(results)

checkpoints.prompt: After both calls — what is results?
With the fix — after both calls, what is results?

why_line: tray=[] was built once, when def ran — both calls append to that same list, so both entries in results are the one list ['pepperoni', 'mushroom'].

explain.rule: The default tray is a single shared tray by the counter — the second pizza picks up the one with the pepperoni still on it, and both receipts point at the same tray.
explain.bridge: So how could each call get a brand-new tray instead of the one by the counter?

fix.rule: Default to None and build the list inside: tray = [] then runs on every call, so every call gets its own.

walk.gloss: No tray given? The default is None — nothing shared.
Check whether a tray was passed in.
If not, build a brand-new empty one — this runs every call.
Add the topping to this call's own tray.

hints: After the second call, look at results[0]. Did it change?
The [] in the def line is built once, not once per call.
Use tray=None, then tray = [] inside when it's None.

follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — one call can't share a tray, so the answer is a single-item list.

one_liner: A default list is built ONCE and shared forever — defaults should be things that never change.
